note: The required set. R3V2-BASE-01 says it is decided here and not by whatever turns up in a results file, so this is the file the verifier reads first and the results are checked against it -- never the other way round.

core.purpose: basic operand collection and SIMD writeback
the tail, a dynamic alpha, the LSU and writeback. grid=2 runs sequentially on one core and is not a claim about two tiles.
tensor -> VRF -> MMA -> store, end to end numerically
two K16 steps; the return-contention baseline
window reuse, concurrent clients, resources returned. C05 is allowed to be slower than C04; if it is, the reason is published and K is not increased to make it look better.
mask, a dependency chain, and read/write destinations

components.what: capacity, banks, the inverse mapping, role aliasing, per-bank port limits

mask, RDW, conflict, back-to-back requests, a stalled read response, against an independent model. Three seeds at the candidate's one-cycle latency; the existing two-cycle component test is retained but is not new work
cold reset, read after a partial write, relaunch, in-flight at reset, zero/write race
the new top instantiates the banked VRF on the live datapath; every client enumerated; no shadow copy
three same-bank sources serialise, cross-bank parallel, no issue before all sources, payload stable across a stalled response
one directed program per read client (simd, lsu, tensor, matrix) that makes it really stall
multiple writers to one bank in one cycle; every accepted transaction commits exactly once; a full FIFO stops issue
the frozen fairness bound under sustained requests; conservation of issued/accepted/returned/committed/cancelled; credits returned
collector entry reuse, flush and fault interleaved with a late return; leases freed on the real last consumption
bank accepted/conflict, collector wait, writeback wait, inflight/credit against a short independent trace

mutations.breaks: the read returns a cycle early, or the wrong bank's data
a writeback reservation is dropped, or a full queue is ignored
after a flush, an old tag writes into a new entry
a masked write is dropped, or a source is freed early
a stall is counted twice, or one accepted request is missed
the model allows unlimited reads from one bank
a missing candidate, an enlarged K, a forged elapsed time, missing evidence

inherited.why: the single-core ISA regression on the unchanged default profile
the same programs under a back-pressuring memory
unit benches; shared RTL changes reach them
every file still elaborates, the new ones included
ownership, footprint and resource checks must not regress
the profile table against what the RTL elaborates, now with a new profile in it
generated artefacts still match their inputs
the real Triton frontend still compiles and runs
the same single-core ISA regression on the candidate. R3V2-REG-01 asks for the inherited cases to run on the candidate too, not only on the profile that did not change.
shared RTL changed, so the four-tile machine runs as well

second_environment.note: A cross-environment smoke, not a second full acceptance. Its runs are budgeted separately and do not combine with the main environment's to make up coverage.
second_environment.compare: numerical results and deterministic counts must agree; wall time is recorded separately and is not compared

mutation_rtl_accounting.why: The clean baseline for every mutation is the component suite passing on the unmutated candidate tree, which is already counted under `components`. Running it a second time to call it a baseline would spend budget to learn nothing.
